_source: CLAUDE.md §45 VALIDATION. The twelve methods and eleven checks below are §45's own lists, in §45's order and wording. scripts/tests/test_validation.py parses them back out of CLAUDE.md.
_reader: scripts/validation.py is the ONE runner. Each method takes an EVALUATOR -- a callable that maps a configuration to a trade population -- so a method can be tested on a synthetic system and run on the real engine without the method knowing which it has.
_the_posture: CLAUDE.md §45: 'Actively attempt to disprove candidates. Do not only search for evidence that a candidate works.' That is a statement about the DEFAULT, so the default here is refutation: `disprove()` returns REFUTED unless every applicable check passes, and a check that could not run counts as NOT SURVIVED rather than as silence. Confirmation is what you are left with after failing to break something, never the starting position.

methods.definition: The candidate measured on the data it was built from. Not validation, and labelled so: it is the baseline every other method is compared against.
The candidate measured on a period declared out-of-sample and not yet used for any choice (§44).
methods._gated_by: §44: this repo currently has NO untouched period, so oos() refuses rather than measuring development data and calling it validation.

methods.definition: Rolling windows: measure each window using only what preceded it. With fixed rules there is nothing to re-fit, so what this tests is whether the edge is STABLE across time rather than concentrated in one stretch.
Vary one parameter around its configured value and measure how the result moves. A result that survives only at its exact setting was fitted to that setting.
Partition the population by market regime and measure each part. An edge present in one regime only is a regime bet.
methods.implemented_by: scripts/validation.py partition() with a regime key

methods.definition: The same rules per instrument. An edge carried by one symbol is that symbol's edge.
methods.implemented_by: scripts/validation.py partition() with an instrument key
scripts/validation.py partition() with a session key

methods.definition: The same rules per year and per quarter.
methods.implemented_by: scripts/validation.py partition() with a period key

methods.definition: The combined verdict over the perturbation family: sensitivity, perturbation, stress and Monte Carlo together.
Resample the trade SEQUENCE to ask what the equity path could have looked like -- the order of the same trades is luck, and a drawdown that depends on it is not a property of the rules.
Jitter the inputs -- entry fills, stop placement -- by a small amount and re-measure. A result that needs an exact fill is a result about a fill nobody will get.
Re-measure under deliberately hostile execution assumptions: a wider fee, slippage against every fill, a worse fill on every stop.

checks.asks: is n large enough for the claim being made?
is the edge spread across the period, or concentrated in a few trades?
does it survive in every regime, or only one?
is it carried by one symbol?
is it carried by one session?
is it carried by one year or quarter?
does it survive hostile fills and costs?
what did §20 say about the series this was measured on?
how many candidates were this one chosen from?
does the instrument set contain only survivors?
how many tests produced this winner?

verdicts.SURVIVED: the check ran and the candidate was not broken by it
verdicts.REFUTED: the check ran and broke the candidate
verdicts.NOT_RUN: the check could not run. NOT a pass: §45's posture is refutation, so a check that did not run counts against the candidate in disprove().

_thresholds_are_the_callers: No threshold in this file. §45 says what to check, not where to draw a line, and a line drawn here would be a project parameter masquerading as a rule. Every check takes its threshold as an argument, records it in the result, and the report shows it -- so a reader can see what 'survived' was measured against and disagree with it.
